nodes.label: Co-Evolution in Agentic Systems: Toward Self-Directed Evolution Beyond Human Design
nodes.author: Qing Zong, Jiayu Liu, Junhao Shen, Zecong Tang, Linsi Wu, Yuxuan Liu, Rui Wang, Zhaowei Wang, Weiqi Wang, Cheng Qian, Xiusi Chen, Yangqiu Song

nodes.label: Co-Evolution in Agentic Systems
nodes.rationale: Central organizing principle: multiple components impose evolutionary pressure on one another, distinguishing mutual adaptation from mere interaction or information exchange

nodes.label: Agent–Agent Co-Evolution
nodes.rationale: First stage: co-evolution within agent collective where each agent's improvement is driven by other evolving agents; includes adversarial, collaborative, and organizational adaptation

nodes.label: Agent–Environment Co-Evolution
nodes.rationale: Second stage: extends adaptation to environmental components (tasks, feedback, interaction spaces); agents reshape environment which then reshapes agents

nodes.label: Meta Co-Evolution
nodes.rationale: Third stage: evolution mechanism itself becomes adaptive; system revises what, when, how, where to evolve and how to evaluate; pathway toward open-endedness

nodes.label: Adversarial Agent Co-Evolution
nodes.rationale: Agents co-evolve through opposing objectives; one agent's progress raises difficulty for opponent; includes pairwise (GAN-like) and multi-source pressure

nodes.label: Collaborative Agent Co-Evolution
nodes.rationale: Agents co-evolve through shared goals; one agent's improvement forces partners to adjust coordination; includes parallel and role-differentiated collaboration

nodes.label: Evolving Agent Organizations
nodes.rationale: Agents co-evolve with organizational structure including role assignments and interaction topology

nodes.label: Task-Space Co-Evolution
nodes.rationale: Environment adapts what problem agent solves next; includes exposure/selection from fixed pool and adaptive task generation

nodes.label: Feedback-Space Co-Evolution
nodes.rationale: Environment co-evolves in how it evaluates/rewards agent behavior; includes preference-driven, outcome-driven, and consistency-augmented feedback

nodes.label: Interaction-Space Co-Evolution
nodes.rationale: Environment adapts where agent acts; includes executable world construction and model-based world construction

nodes.label: Red Queen Effect
nodes.rationale: Biological principle: sustained progress requires mutual adaptation rather than adaptation on only one side; motivates co-evolution over single-entity self-evolution

nodes.label: Open-Endedness in Co-Evolution
nodes.rationale: System continues generating meaningful novelty rather than converging to fixed endpoint; characterized by continuous novelty and unbounded divergence

nodes.label: Self-Refutation Loop
nodes.rationale: Failure mode in long-horizon evolution: system repeatedly concludes experiments fail to support objective yet continues revising same direction

nodes.label: Dynamic Evaluation Challenge
nodes.rationale: Open challenge: evaluating co-evolution requires determining whether all components improve, whether gains transfer to unseen partners/environments, and component contributions

nodes.label: Safety and Governance in Co-Evolution
nodes.rationale: Open challenge: as co-evolution becomes autonomous, humans may lose control; need governance keeping evolution auditable, interruptible, with rollback and intervention points
